presentingComplaint: Sudden-onset right-sided weakness and slurred speech 90 minutes ago
history: Witnessed acute onset at 08:15 of right facial droop, right arm and leg weakness, and difficulty speaking while eating breakfast; last known well clearly documented at 08:00. No headache, no seizure, no vomiting. Background of longstanding hypertension (on amlodipine), type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, and permanent atrial fibrillation for which he was prescribed apixaban but self-discontinued it 3 weeks ago due to a minor gum bleed. Ex-smoker (30 pack-years). No recent trauma or surgery, no anticoagulant taken in preceding 48h.
examination: Alert, GCS 15 but dysarthric with expressive aphasia. Right facial weakness (upper-motor-neuron pattern, forehead spared), right hemiparesis (arm MRC 2/5, leg 3/5) with right-sided sensory inattention and a left gaze preference. NIHSS 12. Irregularly irregular pulse. No neck stiffness, no papilloedema, no thunderclap features. Pertinent negatives: no fever, no meningism, no fluctuating consciousness, no recent head injury, capillary glucose normal.
imaging: Non-contrast CT head: no haemorrhage, hyperdense left MCA sign, early loss of grey-white differentiation in left insula (ASPECTS 8). CT angiography: proximal left M1 middle cerebral artery occlusion. CT perfusion: small core with sizeable penumbra (favourable mismatch).
differentialDiagnoses: Acute ischemic stroke (cardioembolic, left MCA territory)
finalDiagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke - left MCA cardioembolic (AF, anticoagulation lapse)
citations: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke 2019 (2019 update)
contraindications: Confirm no intracranial haemorrhage on CT before thrombolysis
Verify BP <185/110 before IV alteplase/tenecteplase; treat if higher
Recent anticoagulant use / coagulopathy would contraindicate thrombolysis (here apixaban stopped >48h, INR normal)
edgeCases: Stroke mimics (hypoglycaemia, seizure with Todd's paresis, complicated migraine) must be excluded before lysis
Wake-up / unknown-onset stroke may still be eligible via MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch or perfusion imaging
Large-vessel occlusion warrants mechanical thrombectomy up to 24h in selected patients regardless of thrombolysis
expectedMaiK: Classic hyperacute left-MCA cardioembolic ischaemic stroke in an AF patient off anticoagulation, within the thrombolysis window with an LVO - this is a time-critical 'brain attack' requiring immediate stroke-team activation for IV thrombolysis and thrombectomy assessment.
expectedNextQuestions: What is the exact last-known-well time and is the patient within 4.5h for thrombolysis / 24h for thrombectomy?
Any contraindication to thrombolysis (recent surgery, bleeding, anticoagulant timing, BP)?
expectedInvestigations: Urgent non-contrast CT head plus CT angiography (and CT perfusion) to exclude haemorrhage and identify large-vessel occlusion
Capillary blood glucose, coagulation profile and ECG

investigations: Non-contrast CT head with CT angiography

regressionAssertions: differential must include ich (haemorrhagic stroke must be excluded by CT before thrombolysis)
